Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

When you are in the basement of any multi-story buildings like schools, apartments, or even in Mars, you can see some part of the building will be projected below the roofing, just like this, like a horizontal member.

Key details

  • You can see in this picture these horizontal members, those projections, what you can see in the basement, we call them as beams.
  • These beams play very important role in all the structures.
  • Then how to define these beams?
  • We are going to define beam as a structural member which offer resistance to bending at the rotation due to the applied loads.
  • And these beams are usually long prismatic bars and the loads are applied normal to the axis of the bar.
  • The first one is roller support.
  • This is the roller support here.
  • You can see the beam is resting on this roller support.
  • The reason is if you think of applying a.
  • Vertical load here, we can't move the beam along y direction because the roller will restrict the movement of this beam along the y direction.
  • Whereas if you think you are going to apply a horizontal force on this beam like this, definitely it is going to move along the horizontal direction.
  • Because there won't be any restriction from the support onto the movement of the beam along X direction.
  • If you think of applying a couple at this free end, it is free to rotate about this roller support.
  • That's why.
  • Remember whenever we have a roller support, roller will offer resistance for the motion only along y direction, that's why we will be having only one reaction normal to the surface of the contact.
  • This is about roller support.
  • Next one is fixed support.
  • In fixed support, the beam will be like this.
  • It is represented in this way.
  • Beam along y direction.
  • At the same time, if you think of applying a horizontal force on this beam, again the.
  • Support will offer restriction for the motion of the beam along X direction.
  • That's why it will be having two reactions.
  • One will be along X direction, one more will be along Y direction.
  • In the same way, if you think you are going to apply a couple here at the free end R due to the application of the force.
  • Do you think the beam will start to rotate like this about the axis of the beam?
  • No, it won't, because.
  • This will have a resisting couple.
  • Three reactions to our forces, one along X, one more along Y, and one more will be the resisting couple like this.
  • Next one is spin arranged support.
  • This support will offer resistance for the motion of the beam in both along x direction as well as along the y direction.
  • That's why two reactions, one along x direction and one more along y direction.
  • This slide is very important to solve the numericals.
  • Next is different types of beams.
  • We are going to broadly classify the beams as statically determinate beams and statically indeterminate beams.
  • Statically determinate beams.
  • We can find the support reactions using the conditions of equilibrium.
  • And in one more way, if the beam is having just sufficient number of support reactions which are enough for the beam to be in equilibrium.
  • That is also called as statically determinate beam.
  • If the beam is having more.
  • Number of support reactions that necessary for the stable equilibrium configuration that is called as statically indeterminate beam.
  • The first one is simple beam.
  • If one end of the beam is on a pin connection or a hinged connection, and if one end is an roller, that we call it as a simple beam.
  • How many number of support reactions here?

Example or application from the lecture

  • We have different before moving on to the different types of beams, let's know about different types of supports.
  • Ah when we draw the free body diagram in the numericals, if there is a roller support, usually we consider there will be only one reaction from the roller support.
  • Let's talk about statically determinate beams.
